**3. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — HTML injection from the feed's own link.**
**4. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:64,70` — protocol-relative URLs are corrupted.**
**5. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:26` — `NoMethodError` when the embedded post is gone.**
**6. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content` is Atom-only and `scrub` is Ruby 2.1+.**
**7. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-37` — no error handling, no timeouts, one bad item kills the run.**
**8. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28` — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a real header value.**
**10. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — non-atomic throttle can wedge a URL forever.**
**11. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` and `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` — `force: true` in migrations.**

`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-47` asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` while the controller actually calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` — it passes only if jobs run inline in the test env, and it verifies neither the job args nor the `no_throttle`/staff logic. `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs the very private methods under test (`expects(:retrieved_recently?)`), so `perform_retrieve`, the redis throttle, and the `TopicEmbed.exists?` re-check have **zero** coverage. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the three guard clauses and never exercises `poll_feed` — which is where bugs #6 and #7 live. Also untested: `absolutize_urls` (bug #4), `import_remote`, the referer-host rejection path (only the *missing*-referer case is covered), and both new views. **Fix:** at minimum add a `poll_feed` test against a fixture RSS *and* Atom document, and `absolutize_urls` cases for `//host`, `../rel`, `#anchor`, and a non-80/443 port.

**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`** — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison, and `e.source` is never checked against `iframe.contentWindow`. Only `height` is attacker-controllable today, so impact is low, but it should be `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin`.
**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12`** — no null guard on `getElementById('discourse-comments')`; a host page that loads the script above the div gets a `TypeError` and no comments.
**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:22`** — `iframe.height = h + "px"` sets the HTML *attribute*, which takes a bare number; use `iframe.style.height`.

**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7`** — `discourseUrl + "embed/best"` silently requires a trailing slash on `discourseUrl`, and there is no documentation anywhere in the diff telling integrators how to set the two globals. Normalize the slash and add setup docs.

**Asset precompilation** — `embed.js` / `embed.css.scss` are new standalone bundles (`stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`); confirm both are added to the `precompile` list, otherwise this 404s in production. (The relevant config isn't in this diff.)

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`** — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; it will raise on a frozen string and double-appends the footer if the same object is imported twice. Use `contents + ...`.
**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:59`** — `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` is wrong for `https://host:80` / `http://host:443`; compare against `uri.default_port`.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:78`** — `embed_url` is matched exactly with no normalization, so `?utm_source=…`, a trailing slash, or `http` vs `https` each create a separate topic for the same article. The `:string` column also caps at 255 chars, so long URLs will raise on insert.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-31`** — if `creator.create` returns nil the failure is swallowed with no logging, and `loading.html.erb` then reloads every 30s **forever**. Add a give-up/error state and log creation errors.

**`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:10`** — the 30s reload is shorter than the `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` cache on the same response, so the first reload likely re-serves the cached loading page.
**`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20`** — `feed_key` is dead code (an unfinished Last-Modified optimization). Remove or use it.
**`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1`** — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused copy-paste.
**`config/locales/server.en.yml:36`** — `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.
**`db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`** — whitespace-only churn on an unrelated migration, and it now ends without a newline. Four of the new files also lack trailing newlines.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **2. `app/models/post.rb:130` + `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — raw-HTML posts bypass all sanitization (stored XSS).**

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` mode and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) where Discourse would typically sanitize/transform content. `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`), does only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and then calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, so the externally-sourced HTML is stored and later rendered. Additionally, the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` which will output that HTML without escaping. There is no sanitization step in this path (Nokogiri `fragment.to_html` in `absolutize_urls` does not sanitize), so a malicious feed item can persist script tags/unsafe attributes (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **3. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — HTML injection from the feed's own link.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it appends HTML containing `"#{url}"` into `contents` without escaping/sanitizing `url`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute (e.g. `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, this becomes a direct HTML/JS injection vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **4. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:64,70` — protocol-relative URLs are corrupted.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both the `` and `` rewrite logic checks `start_with?('/')` and then strips all leading slashes via `sub(/^\/+/, '')`. For protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/app.js`, this code will treat them as site-relative and rewrite them to something like `http:///cdn.example.com/app.js`, corrupting the URL. This is a concrete, verifiable correctness bug introduced by the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **5. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:26` — `NoMethodError` when the embedded post is gone.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` record is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then (if the content hash changed) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!`. If the associated post has been deleted (or the association otherwise returns `nil`), `post` will be `nil` and `PostRevisor` will blow up when it tries to operate on `@post` (nil), causing a `NoMethodError`. There is no guard here (e.g., handling orphaned `topic_embeds`), and no DB-level foreign key shown in the diff to prevent this orphan state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **6. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content` is Atom-only and `scrub` is Ruby 2.1+.**
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that `i.content` is Atom-only, implying it may be absent for many RSS feeds. This aligns with the golden issue that calling `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is present and can crash when it’s nil. While it doesn’t explicitly mention adding a `description` fallback, it identifies the same root problem (missing `content` field leading to failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **7. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-37` — no error handling, no timeouts, one bad item kills the run.**

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is called with no explicit timeouts or rescue. If the network request hangs/raises (DNS, timeout, SSL, invalid feed), the whole scheduled job will error out. Additionally, inside `rss.items.each` it calls `i.content.scrub` and `i.link`/`i.id` without guarding against nil or malformed item fields; a single item with missing/invalid `content` (nil) would raise `NoMethodError` and abort the entire run because there is no per-item exception handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **8. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28` — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a real header value.**

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The X-Frame-Options header only has standardized values like `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN` (and historically `ALLOW-FROM <uri>` in some browsers). `ALLOWALL` is not a valid value and will typically be ignored by browsers, so it’s a real correctness/security issue: the code intends to control framing behavior but uses a non-standard value that won’t reliably work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **10. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — non-atomic throttle can wedge a URL forever.**

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two commands are not atomic; if the process dies or an exception occurs after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` executes, the key can remain without a TTL. That would cause `setnx` to fail forever for that URL, effectively wedging retrieval permanently. This risk is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **11. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` and `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` — `force: true` in migrations.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `force: true` in `create_table` for `topic_embeds` (new migration) and modifies an existing migration to use `force: true` for `top_topics`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it, which can mask unexpected state and can cause data loss if the table already exists (e.g., a partially-applied migration, manual table creation, or a rollback/re-run). A safer default is to let `create_table` raise if the table exists rather than deleting it. This risk is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **12. `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3` — no rollout plan for the largest table.**

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` adds `cook_method` to `posts` with `default: 1` and `null: false` in a single `add_column`. On PostgreSQL (commonly used by Discourse, and especially in older versions), adding a column with a non-NULL default can rewrite the whole table and take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which is risky for a large/high-traffic table like `posts`. The diff includes no staged rollout/backfill (e.g., add nullable column without default, backfill in batches, then set default + NOT NULL), so the operational risk is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-47` asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` while the controller actually calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` — it passes only if jobs run inline in the test env, and it verifies neither the job args nor the `no_throttle`/staff logic. `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs the very private methods under test (`expects(:retrieved_recently?)`), so `perform_retrieve`, the redis throttle, and the `TopicEmbed.exists?` re-check have **zero** coverage. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the three guard clauses and never exercises `poll_feed` — which is where bugs #6 and #7 live. Also untested: `absolutize_urls` (bug #4), `import_remote`, the referer-host rejection path (only the *missing*-referer case is covered), and both new views. **Fix:** at minimum add a `poll_feed` test against a fixture RSS *and* Atom document, and `absolutize_urls` cases for `//host`, `../rel`, `#anchor`, and a non-80/443 port.

adjudication.rationale: This finding is verifiable from the diff: `EmbedController#best` does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever`; when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and renders `loading`. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` includes a test that expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which does not match the controller code and would fail unless the controller actually invoked `TopicRetriever` (it doesn’t). The other points about limited coverage are also grounded in the diff (e.g., `topic_retriever_spec` stubs `retrieved_recently?`, and `poll_feed_spec` never calls `poll_feed`), but the controller/spec mismatch alone is a clear defect introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`** — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison, and `e.source` is never checked against `iframe.contentWindow`. Only `height` is attacker-controllable today, so impact is low, but it should be `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin`.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using `indexOf` for origin validation is a substring check rather than a proper origin comparison and notes it can be bypassed, recommending `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin`. This is the same core issue as the golden comment about malicious domains passing the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12`** — no null guard on `getElementById('discourse-comments')`; a host page that loads the script above the div gets a `TypeError` and no comments.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the script immediately does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the element is not present yet (e.g., the script is loaded in `<head>` before the target div exists, or the host page omits/misnames the div), `comments` is `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError`, preventing the embed from working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:22`** — `iframe.height = h + "px"` sets the HTML *attribute*, which takes a bare number; use `iframe.style.height`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `embed.js` sets `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px";`. The `height` IDL attribute on `HTMLIFrameElement` reflects the HTML `height` content attribute, which is defined as a non-negative integer (CSS pixels) and is typically set as a bare number/string like "300" (not "300px"). Appending "px" can lead to inconsistent parsing/coercion across browsers (some may ignore non-numeric values or coerce unexpectedly). Using `iframe.style.height = ...` (or assigning a number/string without "px" to `iframe.height`) avoids this correctness risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7`** — `discourseUrl + "embed/best"` silently requires a trailing slash on `discourseUrl`, and there is no documentation anywhere in the diff telling integrators how to set the two globals. Normalize the slash and add setup docs.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. This will produce an invalid path like `https://forum.example.comembed/best` unless `discourseUrl` ends with `/`. The diff does not include any normalization (e.g., ensuring a trailing slash) or any code/docs in this change that define/guarantee the format of the `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals, so the code as introduced is fragile and can break depending on how integrators set `discourseUrl`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Asset precompilation** — `embed.js` / `embed.css.scss` are new standalone bundles (`stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`); confirm both are added to the `precompile` list, otherwise this 404s in production. (The relevant config isn't in this diff.)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new standalone assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`) and a new layout that references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. However, whether this will 404 in production depends entirely on existing asset pipeline configuration outside the diff (e.g., whether `embed.css`/`embed.js` are already covered by `config.assets.precompile`, custom sprockets settings, or other build steps). The diff alone does not show that they are *not* precompiled, so the claimed defect is not strictly verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`** — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; it will raise on a frozen string and double-appends the footer if the same object is imported twice. Use `contents + ...`.

adjudication.rationale: The code does mutate the `contents` argument in-place via `contents << "..."`, but in this diff there’s no verifiable evidence that callers pass a frozen string or reuse the same `String` object across multiple imports in a way that would cause double-appending. Current call sites shown (`PollFeed` assigns a fresh `content` per item; `import_remote` passes freshly-read HTML; specs pass literals without frozen-string behavior) don’t demonstrate an actual failure or incorrect behavior. The finding describes a potential side effect, but not a concrete defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:59`** — `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` is wrong for `https://host:80` / `http://host:443`; compare against `uri.default_port`.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix is built as "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}" and then the port is appended only if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443. This check ignores the URL scheme: for an HTTPS URL explicitly using port 80 (https://example.com:80/...), uri.port == 80 so the code will incorrectly omit ":80" even though 80 is not the default port for https; likewise for an HTTP URL on port 443 it will omit ":443". Using uri.default_port (or comparing against 80 for http and 443 for https) would be correct. This is a verifiable correctness issue in the diff’s logic for generating absolute URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:78`** — `embed_url` is matched exactly with no normalization, so `?utm_source=…`, a trailing slash, or `http` vs `https` each create a separate topic for the same article. The `:string` column also caps at 255 chars, so long URLs will raise on insert.

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact `embed_url` string equality: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` in `topic_id_for_embed`. No canonicalization/normalization (scheme, trailing slash, query params like `utm_*`) is performed, so semantically same articles with different URL variants will not match and will result in separate `TopicEmbed` rows/topics. Additionally, the migration creates `t.string :embed_url` with no explicit limit; in Rails this is typically `varchar(255)`, so sufficiently long URLs can exceed the column size and fail to insert (or be truncated depending on DB/config), which is a concrete defect risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-31`** — if `creator.create` returns nil the failure is swallowed with no logging, and `loading.html.erb` then reloads every 30s **forever**. Add a give-up/error state and log creation errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `embed` is blank it wraps creation in a transaction and does `post = creator.create` but only creates the `TopicEmbed` row if `post.present?`. If `creator.create` returns `nil`/blank (or otherwise fails without raising), the method exits with `post` nil and no embed record, with no logging or error propagation in this method. Separately, `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `topic_id_for_embed` is nil, and `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the page every 30s; there is no retry limit or error state, so if the embed never gets created the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:10`** — the 30s reload is shorter than the `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` cache on the same response, so the first reload likely re-serves the cached loading page.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally, including when it renders the `loading` template. The loading page (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) calls `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds without a forced reload. If `discourse_expires_in` sets cache headers (e.g., `Cache-Control: max-age=60`), the browser/proxy can legitimately satisfy the 30s reload from cache, re-serving the cached loading page until the 60s TTL expires. That makes the 30s polling ineffective on the first retry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20`** — `feed_key` is dead code (an unfinished Last-Modified optimization). Remove or use it.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (building a Redis key based on the feed URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in that file or elsewhere in the provided diff. The polling logic in `poll_feed` does not use it to cache Last-Modified/ETag or to skip work, so as written it is dead/unused code introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1`** — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused copy-paste.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb the job only looks up a user and calls TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve; nothing in this diff references Email::Sender, so require_dependency 'email/sender' appears unused. However, an unused require_dependency is primarily a cleanup/performance nit (extra load/reload tracking) rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`config/locales/server.en.yml:36`** — `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.
